quotes.text: Decide early. Dashboards are for screens, paginated is for paper. If the primary output goes to a printer, jump tools before you waste a sprint polishing a dashboard that will always betray you in the copy room.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a simple, memorable decision rule for dashboards versus paginated reports.

quotes.text: Build a one page prototype here before committing to deeper tooling. Use it as a live spec, align on paper size, headers, footers, and grouping with your stakeholder.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical quick win for validating paginated report requirements.

quotes.text: The thing most people miss is printable width. Your page width minus margins defines a hard limit, exceeded, and you'll get phantom blank pages. Respect the math.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains a common, concrete cause of broken paginated layouts.

quotes.text: If your reporting footprint is growing, Visual Studio stops being developer theater and becomes the control room. You don't just make reports. You ship a reporting product with standards, tests, and releases.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Argues when enterprise tooling for reports becomes worth the overhead.

quotes.text: Prototype in the service to lock paper size, header, footer, and grouping. Move to report builder when you need page control, expressions, and parameters. Productize in Visual Studio when you need multiple reports, shared data sets, and consistent deployment across environments.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarises the staged migration path across the three tools.

takeaways: Power BI dashboards are built for screens; paginated reports based on RDL are the right tool for fixed, print-ready, audit-proof output.
Use the web paginated builder in the Power BI service for quick tabular prototypes and Power BI Report Builder for real page control, charts and parameters.
Move to Visual Studio with Reporting Services projects when you need report suites with shared data sets, source control, CI/CD and governed deployments.
hook: Exporting Power BI dashboards to PDF produces broken, unreliable printouts. This episode helps Power BI developers and report owners choose between the Power BI service builder, Power BI Report Builder and Visual Studio Reporting Services projects to deliver pixel-perfect paginated reports.
